artboards.title: 3 · A circle was clicked — try it

annotations.text:
Three viewer states, left to right.
1 The pointer is not on the diagram. Nothing is drawn on it. The existing footer line stays.
2 The pointer is anywhere on the diagram. Every participant that appears somewhere else shows its count on the box's bottom-right corner, 16px, clear of the top of the diagram. A participant with no other position shows nothing. Moving off the diagram hides them all.
3 A circle was clicked. Hover alone never opens the popover. Escape, or a click outside, closes it.
Artboard 3 works: move the pointer onto the diagram, then click a circle.

Popover content.
Heading: 'Also appears in'. A related diagram can sit on this page or on another page, so the heading names no collection.
Rows: one page per row, page title only, opening that page. A related diagram on the current page is listed first as 'Another diagram on this page' — plain text, no link. The unit of the relation is a diagram and the unit of the list is a page, so on the current page the row states the relation; the page title would repeat what the reader can see. A page that holds two related diagrams is still one row. The count on the circle equals the number of rows.
Left out on purpose: the participant name (the outlined box carries it), the space key, the label variant, internal identifiers, and any sentence about how the relation was found. There is no 'pick a page' instruction — the row is a link and reads as one.

A row promises one thing: it opens the page. Scrolling to the diagram and highlighting it needs a cross-page, cross-iframe protocol that does not exist yet, so nothing in this UI implies it. That is separate work.
Outside this design: whether two participants with the same name are the same real object, and the wording of the footer line, which is unchanged.
